# nxos_igmp (Resource)

This resource can manage the IGMP (Internet Group Management Protocol) configuration on NX-OS devices, including instance settings, per-VRF SSM translations and interface configurations (version, query timers, report policies, state limits, join groups and static OIFs).

### API Documentation

- [igmpEntity](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Layer%203/igmp:Entity/)

- [igmpDom](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Layer%203/igmp:Dom/)

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nxos_igmp" "example" {
  instance_admin_state    = "enabled"
  any_query_destination   = true
  bootup_delay            = 10
  control                 = "stateful-ha"
  flush_routes            = true
  heavy_template          = true
  instance_control        = "rtr-alert"
  enforce_router_alert    = true
  spoof_check             = false
  strict_querier_election = true
  syslog_threshold        = 80
  vrfs = {
    "default" = {
      ssm_translations = {
        "232.1.1.0/24;10.3.3.3/32" = {}
      }
      interfaces = {
        "eth1/10" = {
          admin_state                     = "enabled"
          allow_v3_asm                    = false
          description                     = "My description"
          group_timeout                   = 300
          control                         = "fast-leave"
          immediate_leave                 = true
          name                            = "igmp-if"
          report_link_local_groups        = true
          suppress_v3_gsq                 = true
          version                         = "v3"
          querier_address                 = "10.1.1.1"
          querier_description             = "My querier description"
          last_member_query_count         = 3
          last_member_query_response_time = 5
          querier_name                    = "querier"
          querier_timeout                 = 300
          query_interval                  = 100
          robustness_variable             = 3
          query_max_response_time         = 20
          startup_query_count             = 4
          startup_query_interval          = 40
          querier_version                 = "unspecified"
          report_policy_route_map         = "REPORT_POLICY"
          report_policy_access_group      = true
          state_limit_description         = "My state limit description"
          state_limit_maximum             = 100
          state_limit_name                = "state-limit"
          state_limit_reserved            = 50
          state_limit_reserved_route_map  = "RESERVED_RM"
          join_types = {
            "1" = {
              versions = {
                "3" = {
                  groups = {
                    "239.1.1.2" = {
                      use_static_oif = false
                      sources = {
                        "10.1.1.1" = {
                          use_static_oif = false
                        }
                      }
                    }
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `admin_state` (String) The administrative state of the object or policy. Some NX-OS versions (e.g. 10.6.4) reject modifying this attribute, in which case it should not be configured.
  - Choices: `enabled`, `disabled`
- `any_query_destination` (Boolean) Allow any destination-IP for General Queries.
- `bootup_delay` (Number) Bootup Route Add Delay.
  - Range: `0`-`65535`
- `control` (String) The control state.
  - Choices: `stateful-ha`
- `deletion_policy` (String) What happens on the device when objects managed by the resource are removed. `delete` deletes the object on destroy, including any configuration not managed by Terraform, and deletes single child objects once none of their attributes are configured anymore, unless the device holds other entries below them. `reset` deletes the objects created by the resource on destroy, resets the managed attributes of the objects that already existed and leaves configuration not managed by Terraform in place. `retain` leaves the device unchanged on destroy and only removes the resource from the state. Overrides the `deletion_policy` of the provider, which defaults to `delete`. See the [Deletion Policy](../guides/deletion_policy) guide for details.
  - Choices: `delete`, `reset`, `retain`
- `device` (String) A device name from the provider configuration.
- `enforce_router_alert` (Boolean) Enforce Router Alert.
- `flush_routes` (Boolean) Flush Routes on Restart.
- `heavy_template` (Boolean) Enabling/Disabling IGMP Heavy Template.
- `instance_admin_state` (String) The administrative state of the object or policy.
  - Choices: `enabled`, `disabled`
- `instance_control` (String) Inst Controls.
  - Choices: `flush-on-restart`, `rtr-alert`, `any-query-dest`
- `spoof_check` (Boolean) Enable spoof check for IGMP.
- `strict_querier_election` (Boolean) Consider subnet check for L3 igmp querier election.
- `syslog_threshold` (Number) IGMP table syslog threshold percentage.
  - Range: `1`-`100`
- `vrfs` (Attributes Map) List of IGMP VRF configurations.
  - Map key: `name` - VRF name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vrfs))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The distinguished name of the object.

<a id="nestedatt--vrfs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `vrfs`

Optional:

- `interfaces` (Attributes Map) List of IGMP interface configurations.
  - Map key: `interface_id` - Must match first field in the output of `show intf brief`. Example: `eth1/1`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vrfs--interfaces))
- `ssm_translations` (Attributes Map) List of IGMP SSM translations.
  - Map key format: `<group_prefix>;<source_address>`
  - Key component `group_prefix`: Group prefix.
  - Key component `source_address`: Source address. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vrfs--ssm_translations))

- `robustness_variable` (Number) Robustness Factor.
  - Range: `1`-`7`
- `startup_query_count` (Number) Startup Query Count.

- `state_limit_reserved` (Number) Reserved Multicast Entries.

- `state_limit_reserved_route_map` (String) Reserved Entries Route Map.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to       = nxos_igmp.example
  identity = {}
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema


#### Optional

- `device` (String) A device name from the provider configuration.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Terraform's `import` block requires a non-empty `id` value, so this format cannot be used to
# import nxos_igmp for the default device. Use the `terraform import` command
# below, or identity-based import shown above, instead.
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import nxos_igmp.example ""
```
